facts.title: Turning Interaction History into Execution State: A Runtime Layer for Long-Horizon Coding Agents (Ledger)
facts.event_hint: Ledger: deterministic execution-state runtime layer preventing redundant reads/actions in coding agents
facts.problem: Long-horizon coding agents accumulate hundreds of actions and observations in their trajectories, yet nothing in this record indicates which observations still describe the repository as it currently stands. The model must implicitly infer execution status from raw history, and when this fails, it acts on outdated file contents or re-executes work whose results are still valid. Prior context-management methods (truncation, summarization, pruning) reduce what the agent reads but do not maintain explicit execution state and cannot prevent redundant commands from running.
facts.mechanism: Ledger is a deterministic runtime layer that maintains an online execution ledger alongside the agent's interaction history. The ledger has three components: (1) observation records — track which file portions were actually returned to the agent with local/global change counters; (2) modification state — tracks files and symbols modified by the agent with per-file and global change counters; (3) command records — normalized command representations with operational categories (inspection, search, testing, modification). Two paths apply this state at each step. INFORM path: renders a compact state view (current focus = recently modified files; observation index = observed files/ranges with freshness status) into the model input before action generation. GOVERN path: evaluates each proposed command before execution and returns Allow / Reuse (returns reference to still-valid earlier result, suppressing re-execution) / Nudge (allows execution but warns of likely redundancy). The layer adds ZERO language-model calls and wraps an otherwise unmodified agent. Conservative safeguards: environment configuration, problem reproduction, repair generation/submission, and error-following commands are always allowed; interventions are capped per task; unsupported commands and parse failures default to Allow.

evidence.claim: Ledger raises Pass@1 on all 500 SWE-bench Verified instances: GPT-5 mini 56.2% to 64.2% (+8.0pp, RRU 18.3%) and MiniMax M2.5 75.8% to 81.0% (+5.2pp, RRU 21.5%)
evidence.source_locator: Table 1 and Section 'Resolution' on PDF Page 5-6
evidence.condition: 500 SWE-bench Verified instances, mini-swe-agent v2, McNemar's test p<0.001 (GPT-5 mini) and p<0.01 (MiniMax M2.5); 59 recoveries / 19 regressions (GPT-5 mini)

evidence.claim: Total cost decreases by 28.9% (GPT-5 mini) and 31.8% (MiniMax M2.5); cost per resolved instance falls 37.8% and 36.2%
evidence.source_locator: Table 2: Efficiency totals across all 500 instances on mini-swe-agent v2
evidence.condition: Identical pricing assumptions within each backbone; MiniMax M2.5 uses 53.1% fewer input tokens

evidence.claim: Redundant snippet re-reads reduced by 24.2% (GPT-5 mini: 1,875 to 1,421) and 35.1% (MiniMax M2.5: 5,840 to 3,790)
evidence.condition: Defined as requests for a previously returned file range that has not changed since last observed

evidence.claim: On OpenAI Codex (substantially different agent scaffold, structured tool calls): +3.4pp Pass@1 (74.8% to 78.2%), -24.4% total cost, -33.1% input tokens, -17.9% model calls
evidence.source_locator: Table 3: Integrating Ledger with OpenAI Codex on all 500 SWE-bench Verified, MiniMax M2.5
evidence.condition: Only a Codex-specific adapter and lightweight model-API proxy added; execution ledger, governing policy, and state-view renderer unchanged; McNemar's test p<0.05

evidence.claim: Ablation: govern drives most resolution gain (govern-only 402 vs inform-only 385 resolved for MiniMax M2.5), while inform drives efficiency (inform-only reduces input tokens from 616.7M to 336.4M for MiniMax M2.5)
evidence.source_locator: Table 4: Ablation results over same 500 instances using mini-swe-agent
evidence.condition: Full system (inform+govern) resolves 405; govern captures most resolution gain, inform captures most efficiency gain

facts.evaluation_context: All 500 instances of SWE-bench Verified (Python projects, issue-style bug reports). Primary scaffold: mini-swe-agent v2 (minimal scaffold, Bash commands). Transfer scaffold: OpenAI Codex (structured tool calls). Backbones: GPT-5 mini and MiniMax M2.5 with high reasoning effort. Official SWE-bench test suites for grading. Compared with SWE-Pruner (+1.4pp, RRU 4.8%) and LaMR (+1.2pp, RRU 4.1%) from prior work. Single run per instance.
facts.limitations: Single run per benchmark instance — no run-to-run variance characterization through repeated trials (though gains are statistically significant under McNemar's test). Only SWE-bench Verified evaluated (Python, issue-style) — other languages, larger repos, and different task formats untested. Governing policy is a fixed set of deterministic rules with hand-chosen thresholds — can miss patterns not covered and does not adapt thresholds. Only one primary scaffold (mini-swe-agent); Codex serves as transfer test only. Behavior on frontier or very small models and on more different scaffolds remains open.
facts.project_relevance: Directly addresses project question 1 (reducing repeated Read/Grep in coding agents). The execution-state approach is complementary to code knowledge graphs: Ledger tracks what the AGENT has done (observed/modified/attempted), while CodeGraph/CodeNib track what the REPOSITORY contains. The govern path that returns Reuse for unchanged-file reads is a concrete mechanism for tool-call reduction without model calls — zero inference overhead. The 24-35% reduction in redundant re-reads is directly measurable evidence for the 'Read次数' metric the project tracks. The fact that this is a runtime layer wrapping an unmodified agent makes it deployable alongside any indexing system. The ablation finding (govern for correctness, inform for efficiency) suggests that preventing redundant actions and informing the model of state are distinct levers — both relevant to agent acceleration. The Codex transfer result (+3.4pp, -24.4% cost) shows scaffold-independence.
